evidence.excerpt: Hypoglycaemic episodes in insulin-treated type 2 diabetes patients are associated with significant morbidity but are difficult to predict from laboratory data alone. We constructed a two-source feature set combining 14 routine biochemical markers with 9 patient-history variables including insulin dose, meal regularity score, and prior episode count, recorded for 2,640 outpatients over 36 months. Prediction targets were hypoglycaemic episodes confirmed by glucose monitor readings below 3.9 mmol/L within a 72-hour horizon. Random forests, logistic regression, and naive Bayes were trained on 80% of the data and evaluated on the remaining 20%. The combined feature set improved F1 from 0.48 (laboratory-only) to 0.61 (combined) for random forests. Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) values identified prior episode count, HbA1c, and insulin dose as the three highest-magnitude contributors. Threshold was set at 0.38 rather than 0.5 to increase sensitivity, following the cost analysis agreed with the clinical partner.
